target_observations.summary: The watch retains the first observed declared blocker independently of the bounded transcript tail and continues enforcing the linger grace after that marker ages out.
evidence: tick() stores the first non-null parsed blocker in self._blocker and subsequently falls back to that stored value when the current tail no longer contains the marker.
self._blocker_at is initialized once and is not reset when the marker disappears or reappears, so elapsed grace remains cumulative.
The linger-stop reason incorporates the retained blocker and fire() records the typed stop before invoking the lane kill callback.

target_observations.summary: The tests directly cover blocker retention after tail eviction and live termination/receipt behavior.
evidence: test_evicted_blocker_still_arms_linger_stop replaces the transcript with more than the tail limit after initial observation, then verifies stopping at the original cumulative grace boundary and preservation of the blocker text.
test_lingering_blocked_lane_is_stopped_after_grace verifies the grace boundary at 59 versus 60 seconds.
test_lingering_blocked_lane_is_killed_live_and_receipted verifies the integrated process is stopped and the original declared blocker remains on lane_progress.

counterweight_triage.concern: A blocker emitted and evicted before the watch's first poll cannot be retained.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The change guarantees cumulative retention after observation; eliminating the bounded-tail sampling race would require a different streaming or offset-based log reader and is not evidence of a regression in the reviewed retention logic.

counterweight_triage.concern: The grace interval begins at observation time rather than the exact marker-write time.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The declaration timestamp is unavailable from the transcript, so observation time is the defensible clock boundary; enforcement may be delayed by at most the configured polling cadence.

next_move: Accept the reviewed cumulative blocker-retention change; no corrective action is required within this bounded scope.
non_claims: No workspace state or tests were executed; the verdict is based only on the identity-bound inline semantic payload.
This review does not establish behavior of unreviewed lane-runner or execution code beyond the interfaces exercised or referenced by the supplied tests.
